dossier.purpose: Prometheus Alertmanager is a Go service that receives alerts from clients such as Prometheus over an HTTP API (v2), then deduplicates, groups, routes, silences and inhibits them and sends notifications to configured receivers (18 integrations incl. email, PagerDuty, Slack, generic webhook) (README.md:6; docs/integrations.md:12-29). It ships the `alertmanager` server (embedded Elm web UI for alerts/silences/status, optional HA gossip clustering) and the `amtool` CLI (.promu.yml:7-12; ui/web.go:31). Relevant to the stated needs: no OTLP receiver, privacy filter, metrics/log/trace store, dataset/experiment store, dashboard/exploration tool over such stores, MCP server, Claude Code/Codex integration, or model-serving/GPU code was found in the tree (searches for otlp, mcp, claude, codex, gpu, llama, inference found nothing relevant; 'otlp' occurs only in tracing/tracing.go, go.mod and go.sum). The only OTLP code is an exporter for Alertmanager's own traces (tracing/tracing.go:177-216,242-314). Its own metrics are exposed in Prometheus exposition format at /metrics (httpserver/httpserver.go:29); an experimental, flag-gated event recorder writes its own events to file/webhook/Kafka/stdout (featurecontrol/featurecontrol.go:30; eventrecorder/recorder.go:14-22); its persisted state is only silence and notification-log snapshot files, alerts are not persisted (docs/high_availability.md:366-378). The tree also holds a jsonnet mixin with alert rules and a Grafana dashboard definition for monitoring Alertmanager's own metrics from a Prometheus datasource (doc/alertmanager-mixin/README.md:3-12; doc/alertmanager-mixin/dashboards/overview.libsonnet:13-17).

claims.claim: 'The Alertmanager handles alerts sent by client applications such as the Prometheus server. It takes care of deduplicating, grouping, and routing them to the correct receiver integrations such as email, PagerDuty, OpsGenie, or many other mechanisms thanks to the webhook receiver. It also takes care of silencing and inhibition of alerts.'
Precompiled binaries for released versions are on prometheus.io/download; 'Using the latest production release binary is the recommended way of installing Alertmanager.'
Docker images are available on Quay.io or Docker Hub; example run publishes 127.0.0.1:9093 and the UI/API is then at http://localhost:9093/.
'Building from source requires Go and Node.js (with npm)'; `make build` builds; `make build BINARIES=amtool` builds just one binary.

API v2 is 'fully generated via the OpenAPI project and Go Swagger with the exception of the HTTP handlers themselves'; spec is api/v2/openapi.yaml; 'Clients can be easily generated via any OpenAPI generator'.
APIv2 lives under /api/v2 (prefixed by --web.route-prefix when set); APIv1 was deprecated in 0.16.0 and removed as of 0.27.0.

`amtool` is a CLI for the Alertmanager API, 'bundled with all releases'; also installable with `go install github.com/prometheus/alertmanager/cmd/amtool@latest`; default config files $HOME/.config/amtool/config.yml or /etc/amtool/config.yml.
High availability is 'enabled by default'; both UDP and TCP are needed on the cluster port (0.15+).

HA is configured with `--cluster.*` flags (listen-address default 0.0.0.0:9094, peer, peer-timeout, gossip-interval, pushpull-interval, tcp-timeout, probe-*, reconnect-*, label); `--cluster.listen-address=` (empty) turns HA off.
Prometheus should be pointed at all Alertmanagers, not load-balanced, because every Alertmanager is expected to receive all alerts.

The README makes no statement about OTLP/OpenTelemetry, telemetry, local metric/log/trace storage, dashboards over stores, MCP, Claude Code/Codex, or model serving (README.md, docs/, AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG.md contain no match for otlp/opentelemetry/otel).

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics, usage reporting or update check was found: searching all non-lock files for telemetry/analytics/sentry/update-check terms only hits OpenTelemetry imports (e.g. api/api.go:31, dispatch/dispatch.go:29-33). Non-test code makes no outbound HTTP calls except configured notifiers, cluster peer DNS lookups (cluster/cluster.go:744-760) and the exporters below. The embedded Elm UI has no external resource URLs in ui/app/index.html or vite.config.mjs, and the React UI only calls the Alertmanager API (ui/mantine-ui/src/data/api.ts:61). Inbound: HTTP on :9093 by default (cmd/alertmanager/main.go:63) serving /api/v2, /metrics, /-/reload, /-/healthy, /-/ready and pprof /debug/* without authentication unless the experimental --web.config.file TLS/basic-auth is used (httpserver/httpserver.go:19,28-67; docs/https.md:6-13); HA gossip is on by default at 0.0.0.0:9094 TCP+UDP (app/options.go:31; README.md:338-342) and unencrypted unless --cluster.tls-config is set (docs/high_availability.md:357; cmd/alertmanager/main.go:87). Outbound only where configured: notification receivers (default API base URLs for PagerDuty, OpsGenie, WeChat, VictorOps, Telegram, Webex, Rocket.Chat and Slack at config/config.go:750-757, contacted only if such a receiver is configured; User-Agent carries the Alertmanager version, notify/util.go:39-40); OTLP traces only when a `tracing:` block with `endpoint` exists (gRPC default, HTTP optional, default sampling fraction 0; tracing/tracing.go:108-121,242-314; tracing/config.go:72-92; docs/configuration.md:2105-2111) - Alertmanager is an OTLP client for its own spans and has no OTLP receiver; the event recorder (file/webhook/Kafka/stdout) only with --enable-feature=event-recorder plus an `event_recorder:` block (app/app.go:261-265; docs/configuration.md:2139-2141); amtool calls the --alertmanager.url API (cli/root.go:154). No account or hosted service is needed to run it; credentials are needed only for the chosen receivers. Build-time network: `make build` downloads promu v0.20.0 from GitHub releases via curl if missing (Makefile.common:58-59,391-396), runs `npm ci` for the UI (ui/app/Makefile:43-45) and downloads Go modules; release CI pushes images to Docker Hub, Quay and GHCR with secrets (.github/workflows/release.yml:43-49).

entry_points.what: Server binary `alertmanager`: kingpin flags (config.file, storage.path, data.retention, web.*, cluster.*, enable-feature), SIGHUP reload, calls app.Run (main.go:51-203).
CLI binary `amtool`: calls cli.Execute (cli/root.go:148-188); subcommands alert, silence, check-config, cluster, config, template.
Embeddable runtime: New/Start/Stop/Run wire every subsystem (app/app.go:14-90, 181-536); options in app/options.go.
Mounts HTTP API v2 at <route-prefix>/api/v2/ (handlers api/v2/api.go, spec api/v2/openapi.yaml); v1 paths answer HTTP 410 (api/v1_deprecation_router.go:48-65).
OTLP trace exporter manager (gRPC default or HTTP) for Alertmanager's own spans; active only when the `tracing:` config block is present.
Experimental event recorder fan-out to file (JSONL), webhook, Kafka and stdout outputs; active only with --enable-feature=event-recorder.
Top-level YAML config (global, route, receivers, inhibit_rules, time_intervals, tracing, event_recorder) parsed with yaml.UnmarshalStrict (config.go:131,284-300).

code.architecture: Single Go module github.com/prometheus/alertmanager (go.mod:1). cmd/alertmanager/main.go only parses flags/signals and calls app.Run; app/ owns lifecycle and wiring (app/app.go:181-536): cluster peer, optional event recorder, nflog and silences snapshots under --storage.path (app/app.go:290,324), in-memory alert provider provider/mem (the only provider, AGENTS.md:32), API, tracing manager, and a config coordinator plus reloader that rebuilds routes/receivers/inhibitor/dispatcher on reload (app/reloader.go). Alert flow: HTTP API v2 (api/v2: go-swagger generated server/client/models plus hand-written handlers api/v2/api.go) -> provider/mem -> dispatch/ (routing tree, aggregation groups, Dispatcher, dispatch/dispatch.go:59,104,154) -> notify/ pipeline: gossip settle, inhibit mute, time-active/time-mute, silence mute, then per integration cluster-wait -> dedup (nflog) -> retry -> set-notifies (notify/notify.go:175-183,208-211), with one subpackage per integration (18, AGENTS.md:30). Other modules: cluster/ (hashicorp/memberlist gossip, cluster/cluster.go:222-257), silence/ and nflog/ (state replicated over gossip and snapshotted to disk), inhibit/, matcher/ and pkg/labels, template/, timeinterval/, config/, featurecontrol/ (--enable-feature flags, featurecontrol.go:23-41), tracing/ (OTLP trace export plus otelhttp middleware/transport, tracing/http.go:32-50), eventrecorder/ and kafka/ (experimental event outputs; Kafka is producer-side only, kafka/kafka.go:14-26), httpserver/, ui/ (embeds Elm assets from ui/app/dist, ui/web.go:31), cli/ (amtool), doc/alertmanager-mixin (alerts + Grafana dashboard for Alertmanager's own metrics). ui/mantine-ui is a separate React UI that ui/web.go does not embed and that no Makefile/Dockerfile references (only .github/workflows/ui-ci.yml and dependabot).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:6 - Alertmanager dedups, groups, routes, silences and inhibits alerts sent by clients such as Prometheus and sends them to receiver integrations.
claim_checks.evidence: Pipeline stages and per-integration packages exist: notify/notify.go:175-183,208-211 (gossip settle, inhibit, time-active/mute, silence, cluster-wait, dedup, retry, set-notifies); dispatch/dispatch.go:59,104,154 (Dispatcher); 18 integrations in docs/integrations.md:12-29 and AGENTS.md:30. The only alert-ingest path is the HTTP API v2 (api/v2/openapi.yaml:205-223 POST /alerts; api/api.go:176-191; docs/alerts_api.md:19); no OTLP receiver exists (grep 'otlp' matches only tracing/tracing.go, go.mod, go.sum).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:181-192 - API v2 is generated from OpenAPI except the handlers; served under /api/v2 (with route prefix); APIv1 removed as of 0.27.0.
claim_checks.evidence: api/v2/openapi.yaml:3,18 (swagger 2.0, basePath /api/v2/); generated api/v2/{client,models,restapi} via scripts/swagger.sh:12-14 with hand-written handlers in api/v2/api.go; api/api.go:176-191 mounts <prefix>/api/v2/; api/v1_deprecation_router.go:48-65 answers v1 paths with HTTP 410 'deprecated in version 0.16.0 and removed as of version 0.27.0'.

The README omits --cluster.peer-name (main.go:75), --cluster.tls-config (main.go:87), --cluster.allow-insecure-public-advertise-address-discovery (main.go:88) and gives no default for --cluster.settle-timeout, whose code default is 1m0s (main.go:84).

claim_checks.claim: docs/configuration.md:183-184 and 2100-2128 - optional top-level tracing configuration (client_type, endpoint, sampling_fraction, insecure, tls_config, http_headers, compression default gzip, timeout).
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from docs and wins: top-level key is `tracing` (config/config.go:294) but docs line 184 spells it `traciing`; docs list `http_headers` (docs/configuration.md:2120) while tracing/config.go:61 uses `headers`; docs say compression defaults to gzip (2124) but tracing/config.go:74-76 only defaults client_type=grpc and tracing/tracing.go:261-263,292-294 apply compression only when set; docs show endpoint default empty (2108) but a tracing block without endpoint is rejected (tracing/config.go:82-84). config/config.go:131 parses with yaml.UnmarshalStrict, so the doc spellings would be rejected as unknown fields (code inspection only). claim_checks.claim: docs/configuration.md:2130-2141 - the event recorder is gated behind --enable-feature=event-recorder and silently discards events when the flag is off.
claim_checks.evidence: featurecontrol/featurecontrol.go:30,164-166 define the flag ('Experimental event recorder enabled'); app/app.go:261-265 builds a Recorder only when ff.EnableEventRecorder(), otherwise the zero-value Recorder is used and eventrecorder/recorder.go:61-66,306-312 make it discard events. Outputs file/webhook/Kafka/stdout at eventrecorder/recorder.go:172-203; the bounded 8192-event queue drops events when full (recorder.go:42,327-332).

risks: Scope: no OTLP receiver/privacy filter, no metrics/log/trace/dataset store, no dashboard/exploration tool over such stores, no model-serving/GPU code and no Claude Code/Codex/MCP integration exists in the tree (searched otlp, mcp, claude, codex, gpu, llama/gguf/onnx). Its OTLP code only exports its own traces (tracing/tracing.go:177-216); own metrics are Prometheus-format only (httpserver/httpserver.go:29); persisted state is limited to silence and notification-log snapshots (docs/high_availability.md:366-378); both UIs query only the Alertmanager API (ui/mantine-ui/src/data/api.ts:61).

Maturity/maintenance: pre-1.0 (VERSION:1; config/config.go:290 'Remove before v1.0 release'); breaking changes ship in minor releases (CHANGELOG.md:9,41-44,69-71); the event recorder is experimental and flag-gated (featurecontrol/featurecontrol.go:166), HTTPS/basic auth is documented as experimental (docs/https.md:6-7), cluster TLS is flagged [EXPERIMENTAL] (cmd/alertmanager/main.go:87). Facts on activity: ~8-week release cadence through v0.34 (RELEASE.md:6-18), 0.34.1 dated 2026-09-17 (CHANGELOG.md:3), 8 listed maintainers (MAINTAINERS.md:1-8). The clone is shallow (.git/shallow), so commit/contributor history was not assessed.

Default exposure: the HTTP API, /metrics, POST /-/reload and pprof /debug/* are unauthenticated unless the experimental --web.config.file is configured (httpserver/httpserver.go:19,29,31,65-66; docs/https.md:6-13); the default listen is :9093 (cmd/alertmanager/main.go:63); HA gossip is on by default at 0.0.0.0:9094 TCP+UDP and unencrypted unless --cluster.tls-config is set (app/options.go:31; docs/high_availability.md:357).

Data sensitivity of optional outputs: event recorder payloads carry full alert labels/annotations and silence comment/created_by (eventrecorder/eventrecorderpb/eventrecorder.proto:100-125,260-291) to file/webhook/Kafka/stdout with no redaction option (only URL sanitising for logs, eventrecorder/webhook.go:269-291); Kafka uses PLAINTEXT unless tls_config is set (docs/configuration.md:2288-2289). OTLP trace spans carry alert names, fingerprints, group keys and label values (dispatch/dispatch.go:263-264,547; notify/retry_stage.go:64-66). Both features are off by default (tracing needs a `tracing:` block, sampling fraction 0; event recorder needs the feature flag).
